# Recipe page shows the ingredients first

## Problem Statement

Mobile cooks wait for photos, comments and video before they can read a recipe's ingredient list. Home cooks open a recipe on their phone while standing in the kitchen, often on a weak mobile connection, and today the recipe page loads the full photo gallery, the comments and the video player before the ingredient list appears, so the cook waits with nothing to read. According to the parent vision, 38 percent of mobile visitors leave a recipe page before it finishes loading, and support mail names slowness as the most common complaint.

## Business Alignment

**Job to Be Done:** When I am standing in my kitchen with a recipe open on my phone over a weak mobile connection, I want to read the ingredient list as soon as the page opens, so I can check and gather what I need without waiting for photos, comments or video.

**Impact Map:**
- **Goal:** Fewer mobile visitors leave a recipe page before they can read it (the parent vision's first success criterion; today 38 percent of mobile visitors leave before the page finishes loading).
- **Actor:** Home cook reading a recipe on a phone over a mobile data connection (the vision's target audience).
- **Impact:** The cook starts reading the ingredient list while the photo gallery, comments and video are still loading, instead of looking at a page with nothing to read.
- **Deliverable:** A phone recipe page whose ingredient list starts on the first screen and can be read before the photo gallery, comments and video player have finished loading.

**Alignment checks:**
- Goal traces to the vision's problem statement: YES. The vision names the wait with nothing to read and the 38 percent who leave.
- Actor is in the vision's target audience: YES.
- Impact is observable: YES. Whether the ingredient list can be read while the media is still loading can be seen and timed.
- Deliverable covers one functional area: YES. The ingredient list on the phone recipe page.
- Overlap with sibling stubs: none. Glob `plans/functional/faster-recipe-pages-*.md` matched 1 file, this stub.

## User Stories

**As a** home cook reading a recipe on my phone over mobile data, **I want** the ingredient list to be readable before the photos, comments and video have loaded, **so that** I can start checking my ingredients while the rest of the page is still arriving.

**As a** home cook on a weak or dropping mobile connection, **I want** the ingredient list to stay readable when the photos, comments or video fail to load, **so that** a failed download never stops me from cooking.

**As a** home cook, **I want** the photos, comments and video to still appear once they have loaded, without moving the ingredient text I am reading, **so that** I can see the finished dish and other cooks' tips without losing my place in the list.

The third story stops the first two being met by dropping the media from the page.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every scenario uses these terms.

- **Reference phone:** a 360 × 640 pixel screen on a mobile connection throttled to 1.6 Mbit/s download and 150 ms round-trip time, with nothing from the recipe site cached on the phone.
- **Test recipe:** a recipe with 12 ingredients, a photo gallery of 5 photos, 20 comments and a video, unless the scenario says otherwise.

Story 1: ingredients readable before the media has loaded

- [ ] **Scenario: Ingredients appear while photos, comments and video are still loading**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone
  And the test recipe's photos, comments and video are still downloading
  When the cook opens the test recipe
  Then all 12 ingredients are shown as text the cook can read
  And the cook did not wait for any photo, comment or the video to finish downloading

- [ ] **Scenario: Ingredients are readable within 2.5 seconds**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone
  When the cook opens the test recipe
  Then all 12 ingredients are shown as text the cook can read within 2.5 seconds of opening the page

- [ ] **Scenario: Ingredient list starts on the first screen**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone
  And the recipe has 30 ingredients, more than fit on one screen
  When the cook opens the recipe
  Then the heading of the ingredient list and the first ingredient are visible without scrolling
  And the cook can read all 30 ingredients by scrolling down, without waiting for any photo, comment or the video to finish downloading

Story 2: ingredients stay readable when the media or the connection fails

- [ ] **Scenario: Photos, comments and video fail to load**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone
  And the test recipe's photos, comments and video all fail to download
  When the cook opens the test recipe
  Then all 12 ingredients are shown as text the cook can read within 2.5 seconds of opening the page
  And no error message or loading indicator covers any part of the ingredient list

- [ ] **Scenario: Connection drops after the ingredients appeared**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone is reading the test recipe's ingredients
  And the photos, comments and video are still downloading
  When the phone loses its connection
  Then all 12 ingredients stay on screen as text the cook can read
  And the recipe page is not replaced by a blank page or an error page

Story 3: the media still arrives without moving the text being read

- [ ] **Scenario: Photos, comments and video still appear once loaded**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone has opened the test recipe
  When the photos, comments and video finish downloading
  Then the cook can view all 5 photos, read the comments and start the video on the recipe page

- [ ] **Scenario: Arriving media does not move the ingredient being read**
  Given a home cook on the reference phone is reading the test recipe's ingredient list, with one ingredient at the top of the screen
  When a photo, the comments or the video player finishes loading
  Then that ingredient stays at the same place on the screen, moved by 0 pixels

## Scope

### In Scope
- On the phone recipe page, the ingredient list can be read without waiting for the photo gallery, comments or video player to finish loading, within 2.5 seconds on the reference phone (scenarios "Ingredients appear while photos, comments and video are still loading" and "Ingredients are readable within 2.5 seconds").
- The start of the ingredient list on the first screen of the phone recipe page, with the rest reachable by scrolling (scenario "Ingredient list starts on the first screen").
- The ingredient list staying readable when the photos, comments or video fail to download or the connection drops (scenarios "Photos, comments and video fail to load" and "Connection drops after the ingredients appeared").
- Photos, comments and video still shown once loaded, without moving the ingredient the cook is reading (scenarios "Photos, comments and video still appear once loaded" and "Arriving media does not move the ingredient being read").

### Out of Scope
- Desktop layout of the recipe page: excluded by the parent vision's Scope section.
- Search page: excluded by the parent vision's Scope section.
- Recipe editor used by authors: excluded by the parent vision's Scope section.
- Showing the cooking steps ahead of the photos, comments and video: the vision names only the ingredient list, and no stub covers it. Whether to add one is the owner's decision.
- Making the photos, comments or video themselves download sooner: the vision asks that the cook can read without waiting for them, not that they load sooner, and no stub covers it. Whether to add one is the owner's decision.
- Choosing a target value for the share of mobile visitors who leave (38 percent today): this is a business key performance indicator. The owner decides it in the Product Loop, outside this technical pipeline.

## Risks

### Technical Risks
- Page assembly may need restructuring: the vision says the ingredient list appears only after the gallery, comments and video player load, which suggests the page waits for all its content before showing any of it. Separating the ingredient list from that wait may be more than a small change. This project directory holds no page source code to check: Glob `**/*` over the project root matched 4 files (the vision, this stub, its status file and one agent definition). How the page is built today is therefore unknown.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Measure how long the current page takes to show the test recipe's 12 ingredients on the reference phone, and locate where the page waits for the media, before the implementation plan is written. Hand both findings to the implementation planner.
- Arriving media moves the text being read: if no space is kept for the photos and the video, each photo that arrives pushes the ingredient list down while the cook reads.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Test the scenario "Arriving media does not move the ingredient being read" with an automated browser test at phone size. The test records the ingredient's position on screen before and after each photo, the comments and the video player finish loading.

### Business Risks
- The 2.5-second target and the reference phone are the Product Owner's choice, not the owner's: the vision gives no number and no baseline was measured. 2.5 seconds mirrors the threshold Google rates "good" for Largest Contentful Paint. The 1.6 Mbit/s, 150 ms connection may be better than the kitchen connections the vision calls weak.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Review the 2.5-second target and the reference phone with the owner at this plan's approval. Replace both with his numbers if he names others.
- The first-screen requirement pushes the dish photo down: the scenario "Ingredient list starts on the first screen" reads the approved stub title "shows the ingredients first" as first on screen as well as first in time. The vision itself states only the time requirement. Meeting it on a 360 × 640 screen may mean the first screen no longer leads with the photo of the dish.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Present this scenario to the owner at approval as a separate decision. Removing it leaves the other six scenarios unchanged.

### Dependency Risks
- The success measure counts full page load: the vision's 38 percent counts mobile visitors who leave a recipe page before it finishes loading. After this feature, a cook who reads the ingredients and leaves before the photos, comments or video finish loading is still counted as leaving, so the figure can understate the feature's effect. Measuring the effect depends on the analytics behind that figure, which this plan does not control.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Raise with the owner at approval that the success measure needs a version based on when the ingredient list becomes readable. Choosing the measure is his decision, made in the Product Loop.

## Priority

**Priority: HIGH** (Score: 7/9)
- Dependency: 2. No other stub depends on this one and it depends on none. It is the vision's only stub (Glob `plans/functional/faster-recipe-pages-*.md` matched 1 file), so the "parallel" row is the nearest fit.
- Business Impact: 3. It delivers the vision's second success criterion directly and is the vision's route to its first.
- Technical Risk: 2. Moderate: it needs no new technology, but the page may need restructuring (see Technical Risks).
